title: Cost allocation tags, Cost Categories and the resource nobody owns

videos.script: A bill arrives as a total. It does not say whose the money was, and a cost nobody owns grows until somebody finds it. {{whose}} The answer is tags, three keys written down and applied where resources are created. And one fact people learn too late: a tag counts for cost only from the day it is activated, never before. {{tags}} You will find the resources with no owner, and meet the blind spot of the tagging API: it cannot see a resource that was never tagged. {{blind}} Then a month of the shop's bill, read by owner and by usage type. More than a quarter of it belongs to nobody. {{bill}} Part of that is resources someone forgot to tag. Part is cost no tag can ever reach, like data transfer. For that, a Cost Category divides it among the teams, in proportion. And the rest stays visible, under its own name, until somebody owns it. {{split}}
